verses.text: How miserable I am! I am like someone gathering summer fruit after the harvest, picking over the vineyard after the grapes are gone. There is no cluster of grapes to eat, none of the early figs I long for.
Faithful people have disappeared from the land. There is not one honest person left. Everyone waits in ambush to shed blood. They hunt each other with nets.
Their hands are skilled at doing evil. The ruler demands gifts, and the judge accepts bribes. Powerful people tell others what they want, and they all plot together.
The best of them is like a thornbush. The most honest is worse than a hedge of thorns. The day your watchmen warned about has come, the day of your punishment. Now is the time of their confusion.
Do not trust a neighbor. Do not rely on a friend. Even with the woman who lies in your arms, be careful what you say.
For a son treats his father with contempt, a daughter rises up against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A person's enemies are the members of their own household.
But as for me, I will watch for the LORD. I will wait for God my Savior. My God will hear me.
Do not gloat over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will get up. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.
Because I have sinned against him, I will bear the LORD's anger until he takes up my case and wins justice for me. He will bring me out into the light, and I will see him make things right.
Then my enemy will see it and will be covered with shame, the one who said to me, "Where is the LORD your God?" I will see her downfall. She will be trampled like mud in the streets.
The day for rebuilding your walls will come. On that day your borders will be extended.
On that day people will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, from Egypt to the Euphrates River, from sea to sea and from mountain to mountain.
But the earth will become a wasteland because of the people who live there, as a result of what they have done.
LORD, shepherd your people with your staff, the flock that belongs to you. They live alone in a forest, in the middle of fertile pastureland. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as they did long ago.
"As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show them my wonders."
The nations will see and be ashamed, in spite of all their power. They will put their hands over their mouths, and their ears will become deaf.
They will lick the dust like a snake, like creatures that crawl on the ground. They will come trembling out of their hiding places. They will turn in fear to the LORD our God and be afraid of you.
Who is a God like you, who forgives sin and overlooks the rebellion of the survivors of his people? You do not stay angry forever, because you love to show faithful love.
You will again have mercy on us. You will trample our sins underfoot and throw all our wrongs into the depths of the sea.
You will be faithful to Jacob and show faithful love to Abraham, as you promised our ancestors with an oath long ago.
